newsitem.title: USA: Gateway 2000 sees relatively flat margins.
newsitem.headline: Gateway 2000 sees relatively flat margins.

text.p: Gateway 2000 Inc, which posted a 50 percent rise in fourth-quarter net income, said it expects margins in 1997 to remain relatively flat in relation to 1996 levels.
The company said it will continue to strive to achieve its goal of net income equal to five percent of revenues.

Gateway said its gross margins in the fourth quarter hit 19.5 percent -- a record high for the company. It attributed the higher than normal margins to a favorable product mix, particularly the strong demand for Pentium Pro processors and the company's ability to ship the product in quantity throughout the quarter.

The computer maker said its selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expenses are expected to increase in total dollars in 1997 as the company continues its infrastructure investments in customer support, international expansion and aggressive marketing programs.

However, as a percentage of sales, Gateway said it expects 1997 SG&A will be flat to slightly lower. In the fourth quarter, SG&A expenses increased by 23 percent over the third quarter as a result of increased business activity, but due to strong seasonal sales, operating expenses as a percentage of revenues dropped to 11.3 percent from 11.9 percent in the third quarter.
Earlier Thursday, Gateway 2000 reported its fourth-quarter earnings rose to $1.12 a share from $0.74. Sales advanced to $1.55 billion from $1.25 billion.
